Expectation1: Provide guidance and wisdom based on life experience
Situation1: A grandchild directly asks their grandparent for help and advice with a serious concern in their life.
Expectation2: Ensure client satisfaction and address any concerns or complaints professionally
Situation2: A first-time visitor looks disappointed with the colour tone in the mirror.
Story: I was halfway through trimming my client’s bangs when my phone buzzed in my apron pocket. I glanced at the screen and saw my granddaughter’s name, her message reading, “Can I call you? I really need your advice.” My heart squeezed. She never reached out like this unless it was serious. But in my chair sat a first-time client, frowning at her reflection, her lips pressed tight as she eyed the new hair color. I could sense her disappointment, the way she kept tilting her head and sighing. I knew I needed to address her concerns, reassure her, maybe even fix the color if she asked. That was my job—to make sure every client left happy, to listen and respond with patience and skill. But my granddaughter’s message tugged at me, the unspoken expectation that I’d be there for her, offering the wisdom and comfort only a grandparent could give. I felt torn, my hands trembling slightly as I set down the scissors, caught between the needs of the person in my chair and the voice of family reaching out for help.
